A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods and research objectives. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic classification and regression experiments, LoRA evaluations on eight commonsense benchmarks, and supplementary noise-strength experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds rank-256 LoRA results for both Llama models in Table 1.

M1.justification: The MFLD updates, parallel MFNN training, ensemble averaging and noisy-AdamW LoRA merging procedure are unchanged. The revised mathematical analysis does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use double-circle classification, multi-index regression and the same eight commonsense benchmarks. The additional LoRA rank configuration does not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a single rank-256 LoRA comparator for each Llama model. The existing best-of-eight rank-32 comparator remains, relabeled from 'LoRA (best)' to 'LoRA (32, best)'; Appendix Table 3 retains its comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds a comparison between M=1, N=256 and the existing M=8, N=32 ensemble, holding total rank MN=256 fixed. This introduces an additional control configuration; the existing training settings, synthetic protocols and appendix experiments are retained.

E4.justification: The added rank-256 control examines whether merging retains an advantage when compared with one adapter of equal total rank. The existing ensemble-size, neuron-count and noise-strength analyses in Figure 1 and Appendix B are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain Algorithm 3's 50 subset resamplings, Appendix B.2's averaging across 20 networks, and Appendix B.3's best and mean results across eight adapters. No new uncertainty estimates, seed reporting or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds two rank-256 result rows, with average accuracies of 61.28 for Llama2-7B and 84.99 for Llama3-8B. All original results remain unchanged, including PoC-merge averages of 82.74 and 87.30, both figures, and Tables 2–3. These are additional configuration results, not improvements to previously reported scores.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds the conditional/proximal Gibbs identity and replaces Example 1's derivative-bound argument with alpha=alpha0 exp(-2LR^2/(lambda N)). An entropy-sandwich inequality implicit in v1's proof becomes an explicit lemma with a reworked Appendix A.1 derivation. Section 4.1 also derives an optimal ensemble size under fixed total neurons. Theorems 1–4 retain their statements.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims: improved PoC bounds, pointwise and uniform model approximation guarantees, theoretically motivated ensembling, and empirical applicability to LoRA. Additional derivations and comparison results support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the general comparison with single-network training by a fixed-total-neuron tradeoff: increasing ensemble size helps while one error term dominates, but an interior allocation minimizes the bound. Section 3 also explains the finite-particle entropy-sandwich interpretation. The stated limitations concerning lambda approaching zero and LoRA lying outside the theory remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 explicitly documents M=1, N=256 and MN=256 for the added control. Other implementation disclosures, Appendix B's pseudocode and hyperparameters, and the statement that code will be released later are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang (2024), acknowledging prior conditional Gibbs distributions with a Poincare inequality. It removes Bakry et al. (2014) and Brigati and Pedrotti (2024) following the changed LSI argument, and explicitly connects its entropy sandwich to previously cited work. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Explanations in Sections 3 and 4.1 are expanded, Appendix A.1 is reorganized around two lemmas, acknowledgements are added, and citation formatting changes. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from two to three rows per model, adds explicit rank labels, and moves from page 8 to page 9. Figure 1 changes column placement through reflow. Both plotted figures and the appendix tables retain their displays and contents.

improvement.justification: The total-rank-matched LoRA control strengthens the empirical comparison, while the Gibbs-distribution connection and fixed-budget analysis clarify the theoretical justification. These are incremental gains because the main theorems, method and original results remain unchanged. A small drawback is that the new infinite-particle entropy-sandwich display omits the lambda factor implied by its finite-particle counterpart.
